micah: noticed a ~12–18m bump in 4xx for /v1/generate starting ~20:08 UTC — spike is mostly 429 with a handful of 408s. Can someone point to the dashboards/queries for traces + logs so I can add examples to the incident? Also need a quick curl that reproduces the 408 if possible. cc @oncall
sre-alert-bot: :rotating_light: Alert fired: route=/v1/generate 4xx_rate > 5% (15m). ID INC-2026-4532. Grafana: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/route-error-overview/route-errors
tara: Dashboards: Grafana "Route Error Overview" (dash /d/route-error-overview) and "Inference Queues" (/d/infra/inference-queues). For logs use Kibana: `http.request.path.keyword:\"/v1/generate\" AND http.response.status_code:[400 TO 499]` then sort by @timestamp desc. Look for fields trace.trace_id, request_id, upstream_time_ms, gpu_queue_ms, client_ip.
jorge: Quick checklist for triage: 1) check GPU queue/backpressure on the inference-queues dash, 2) check prefix/KV cache miss spikes on the model-serving dash, 3) cluster by client_ip to see rate-limited callers. For alerts: consider adding `group_by: [route, client_ip]` and increasing debounce to 5m while we investigate to reduce noise.
olivia: Example curl that has reproduced the 408 for me using a short client timeout (this forces the client-side 408 when upstream is slow):
```
curl -v -X POST "https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate" \\n  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \\n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \\n  --data '{"prompt":"test","max_tokens":1024}' \\n  --connect-timeout 2 --max-time 7
```
micah: that helps — can you paste 2–3 trace_ids from the spike window so SRE can jump straight to spans? Also which log fields are most useful to paste in the ticket (headers, upstream timings, any specific tags)?
tara: Grab trace.trace_id, http.request_id, http.response.status_code, upstream_time_ms, gpu_queue_ms, and client_ip. Example trace ids from the window: `d2f9a1b47c3e9f00`, `e7b4c23a91f02a11`. In Jaeger/Tempo use: `service=frontend AND http.path:\"/v1/generate\" AND duration>200ms AND status_code=408` — that'll surface traces with upstream timeouts. Also check the nginx access logs (proxy_upstream_time) for slow upstream hints.
micah: copying those into the incident. I'll run the Kibana query + sample curl and attach traces. If client_ip clustering shows a single offender I'll ask infra to mute at the firewall for the short term. :thumbsup:
